transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-12
Start: 10:00 AM PT
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Rajiv Patel (CISO, Sunrise), Laura Gomez (Eng Manager), Ethan Wu (DevOps), Sneha Iyer (Security)

Summary:
Quick review of recent pen test findings that Redwood commissioned as part of the enterprise onboarding scoping. Discuss severity buckets, remediation timelines, integration with Sunrise patching cadence, and implications for SOC2/ISO audit evidence. Agreed to share full report and mitigation playbook, customer to prioritise assets, schedule retest in ~4 weeks.

Topics Mentioned:
- Pen-test findings: dependency vulnerabilities, misconfigured RBAC, audit-log gaps
- Vulnerability management & patch cadence (30/90/365 days debate)
- Secure SDLC: dependency scans, pre-deploy gates, SCA and IaC scanning
- Encryption/KMS and key management concerns for dedicated vs private deployments
- Audit logs, retention and access controls, SSO/SAML and least privilege

Transcript:
00:00 Maya Chen: Okay, thanks everyone for joining, uh we, we'll give about 40, 50 minutes and run through the pen test results, the remediation plan, and then talk about patching cadence and SDLC integration, ok?
00:08 Rajiv Patel: Yep, thanks. Appreciate the summary you sent earlier. I skimmed the executive summary, but we need to go into the vuln list.
00:15 Liam O'Connor: Cool, I'll take the first pass through the technical findings, um note that some of the labels in the automated report are a little fuzzy — like the scanner flagged a number of transitive deps as direct, so we'll clarify that.
00:30 Laura Gomez: Perfect, that's helpful. Our ops team saw a couple items flagged as high that looked like configuration drift though, so interested where you landed.
00:38 Liam O'Connor: Right, item one — dependency vuln (CVE-2025-XXXX) in the jwt library used in the serving runtime. Scanner marked it high cause of chaining with older mac lib — the realistic exploitability is medium in our view because the attack path requires unauthenticated upload to function, which your front-door doesn't allow, but patching's recommended. We're proposing a staged rollout: patch lower risk canaries, run integration tests, then full rollout.
01:05 Ethan Wu: Quick q — what's the recommended rollback plan if the patched runtime causes latency regressions? We can't afford 2x token latency during business hours.
01:12 Liam O'Connor: Good point. We have canary + traffic split controls in the Redwood Dedicated control plane; you can split by route/model. Rollback is a single-button revert for the model variant and the kernel selection. There was a note in the report where the scanner said "kernel mismatch" which is mostly a labeling mismatch in the orchestration logs.
01:30 Sneha Iyer: On RBAC, the pen test highlighted a few service accounts with excessive privileges — read/write on audit buckets. We have SSO/SAML enforcement but need role hardening. Is there a way to get RBAC templates from you?
01:42 Maya Chen: Yes, we have RBAC best-practices templates and a hardened policy pack for enterprise customers. Liam can share the playbook; it includes least-privilege roles for the control plane, KMS-only roles for key ops, and an example policy for audit log access.
01:55 Liam O'Connor: I'll attach the policy examples. Also note that some of the audit log gaps were about retention and cross-region replication. The pen tester found that logs rotated before a particular incident window because retention policy default was shorter in one region — configurational drift again.
02:15 Rajiv Patel: Data residency is a must for us — some of our PII must remain in East US data centers. Does the Redwood private option give us that guarantee?
02:24 Maya Chen: The private deployment (VPC) can be deployed in your chosen region and with customer-managed networking. For strict residency we recommend Private with customer-managed KMS so keys never leave your control. We'll include the architecture diagram in the follow-up.
02:40 Laura Gomez: On encryption, the pen test flagged a key rotation practice — they said keys were rotated yearly by default, which they marked as long. We need to align on rotation cadence and HSM usage.
02:51 Liam O'Connor: We support KMS integrations (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, GCP KMS) and HSM-backed keys for on-prem. Rotation policies are customer-configurable and can be enforced via our IaC modules. The report suggestion was to move to 90-day rotation for some ephemeral keys; for master keys we recommended quarterly rotation only if your compliance requires it — otherwise documented multi-year rotation with strong wrapping is common.
03:20 Ethan Wu: About vulnerability management — we run a 30-day patch SLAs for critical infra. The report recommended 14 days for criticals. We're worried about app-level regressions. Can Redwood support coordination windows or pause updates during our freeze windows?
03:35 Maya Chen: Yes — Redwood supports maintenance windows and scheduled patching. For Dedicated customers we can coordinate patch windows and can pin model versions for latency-critical routes. Also masking, like we can do KV cache warm starts to reduce cold-start penalty after a patch.
03:50 Sneha Iyer: There's also the SDLC ask — the pen test noted lack of dependency scanning during CI for a subset of internal build pipelines. We have SCA but not for the infra code that builds the runtime images.
04:05 Liam O'Connor: Recommended flow: add SCA at PR time, add IaC scanner for Terraform, and include a pre-deploy gate that blocks images with high sev vulnerabilities. Redwood's onboarding doc includes an example GitHub Actions workflow and Terraform checks. We'll share that.
04:20 Rajiv Patel: For audit evidence — SOC2/ISO, we need logs showing who accessed what keys and who changed policies. Is there an exportable audit log we can ingest into our SIEM?
04:33 Maya Chen: Absolutely — we provide syslog/CloudWatch/Stackdriver export options and an API for audit extracts. Logs include actor, resource, action, and before/after snapshots for policy changes. We can sign an SLA for log retention as part of the private contract.
04:50 Laura Gomez: The pen test also called out a misconfigured CORS header on one sandbox endpoint, low severity but easy fix. Was that on Redwood or our integration?
04:58 Liam O'Connor: That was in your integrator config — sandbox endpoint defaults are permissive for dev; for prod we recommend explicit allowlist. We marked it as low but high signal.
05:15 Rajiv Patel: OK, can we walk through the high/critical list and timelines quickly?
05:22 Liam O'Connor: Sure — critical/high: CVE-2025-XXXX (jwt dep) — mitigation: upgrade lib and rotate tokens, suggested timeline: 7–14 days for canary, 21 days full rollout. Second: RBAC service-accounts vector — mitigation: apply least-priv policy and rotate keys, timeline: 14 days. Third: audit log retention gap — mitigation: increase retention and enable cross-region replication, timeline: 3–7 days if it's just config.
06:05 Ethan Wu: Those timelines sound reasonable. For the jwt upgrade, will there be schema bumps we need to change in our client?
06:13 Liam O'Connor: No client-level breaking changes expected; we tested backwards compat on our SDKs. But we'll provide a compatibility matrix.
06:25 Sneha Iyer: For the retest — do you run an internal validation or do we need to coordinate an external third-party retest?
06:33 Maya Chen: We typically do an internal verification for low/medium fixes, and for critical fixes we recommend an external retest. Redwood can coordinate a vendor retest if you want; otherwise we can supply the remediation evidence for your third-party vendor.
06:50 Rajiv Patel: Cost question — retest vendor, does Redwood absorb any of that?
06:55 Maya Chen: Not typically included in the standard onboarding but we're open to discuss as part of the customer success package for enterprise customers. I'll flag that to our CS team.
07:10 Laura Gomez: A couple of practical asks: a remediation playbook for the top 5 findings, an export of audit logs for the last 90 days, and a pinned model variant for two latency-critical routes during patching.
07:22 Maya Chen: Noted. Those are reasonable. We'll attach the playbook, the logs export steps, and instructions for pinning model variants.
07:35 Liam O'Connor: Also going to include example PR checks for dependency scans and an example Terraform policy to prevent open S3/buckets.
07:45 Ethan Wu: Thanks. One last thing — our patching cadence: we run OS image rotation every 90 days, app-level deps every 30 days unless critical. We need to know how Redwood's runtime patches interact with our image rotation, and whether we can decouple them.
07:58 Liam O'Connor: You can decouple — for Dedicated we can schedule runtime patches independently of your node OS image rotation; for Private you control the images so it's fully decoupled. We'll document the interaction matrix.
08:15 Rajiv Patel: Great. Let's recap next steps.
08:18 Maya Chen: Recap: Redwood to share full pen-test report + remediation playbook by 2026-03-15; Liam to share policy templates and CI examples by 2026-03-19; Sunrise to send patching cadence and prioritized asset list by 2026-03-18; schedule retest/check-in for 2026-04-09.
08:38 Rajiv Patel: Sounds good. Thanks everyone.
